DesignComplexSurvival

DesignComplexSurvival computes the operating characteristics of two-group time-to-event trials analyzed with the log-rank test, without patient-level simulation:

  • each group follows a multistate model (progression-free, progressed, switched, dead, and progression-free after a switch before progression) with piecewise constant intensities, covering progression-free survival, overall survival and treatment switching before, at or after progression, with the post-progression intensities measured from progression or from randomization, and the effect of a switch on the death hazard (measured on the post-progression clock or from the switch) or as an accelerated failure time effect;
  • switching may start at a calendar time, for example after an interim analysis (for the OS statistic);
  • accrual is piecewise uniform (by rates or by proportions), dropout is piecewise exponential by group, and PFS may have a censoring of its own and be censored at a switch before progression;
  • expected events, the mean, variance and covariance of the log-rank statistic over calendar time, group sequential bounds by alpha and beta spending (binding or non-binding futility), power, type I error, and the number of events, sample size, accrual duration or follow-up for a target power;
  • progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) can be tested together with a group sequential fixed-sequence or Bonferroni procedure, the latter with recycling of the level after a rejection (Maurer and Bretz 2013), with analyses driven by the events of either endpoint or by calendar time; the joint distribution of the two log-rank statistics gives the power of each endpoint, the probability of rejecting both or at least one hypothesis, and the familywise error rate.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gosukehommaEX/DesignComplexSurvival")

Documentation

The articles on the package website (https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/) cover the workflow of a design, the multistate model and treatment switching, group sequential designs and the covariance of the statistics, PFS and OS tested together, switching from a calendar time, and the validation of the package.

Examples

A delayed treatment effect: the hazard ratio is 1 for 6 months and 0.65 afterwards. The number of events for 90 percent power with interim analyses at 50 and 75 percent of the events:

library(DesignComplexSurvival)
lam <- log(2) / 12
scn <- ms_scenario(
  control = ms_model(death = lam, dropout = 0.003),
  treatment = ms_model(time = c(0, 6), death = c(lam, 0.65 * lam), dropout = 0.003),
  accrual = ms_accrual(time = c(0, 3), rate = c(10, 30))
)
ms_size(scn, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 0.75, 1)),
        test = ms_test(futility = "beta", sf_fut = "HSD", param_fut = -2),
        power = 0.9, solve_for = "events", n = 700)
#> Solved for the final number of events: 587.802 (target power 0.9)
#> 
#> Group sequential log-rank design
#>   Tested endpoint: OS; looks driven by OS events
#>   Sample size: 700; accrual duration: 25.33; final analysis at: 58.66
#>   Power: 0.9001
#>   Type I error: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.02482 (binding)
#>  look  time events info_frac z_upper  p_upper hr_upper z_lower hr_lower
#>     1 25.45    294      0.50   2.963 0.001525   0.7078 -0.5039   1.0605
#>     2 35.51    441      0.75   2.359 0.009162   0.7988  0.7166   0.9340
#>     3 58.66    588      1.00   2.014 0.022000   0.8469  2.0141   0.8469
#>  prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>     0.06203    0.02689   0.06203
#>     0.46398    0.02760   0.52601
#>     0.37413    0.04536   0.90014

PFS and OS tested together: PFS and OS are exponential in both groups (the model of Fleischer et al. 2009), with medians of 4 and 12 months in the control group and 6 and 16 months in the treatment group. PFS is tested at 300 PFS events, where OS is also tested, and OS again at 220 OS events. OS is tested only after PFS has been rejected (fixed sequence):

fl <- ms_scenario(
  control = ms_fleischer(median_pfs = 4, median_os = 12),
  treatment = ms_fleischer(median_pfs = 6, median_os = 16),
  accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 25)
)
ms_power(fl, n = 450,
         looks = ms_looks(c("pfs", "os"), fraction = c(1, 1),
                          test = list(c("pfs", "os"), "os")),
         test = ms_test(endpoints = c("pfs", "os"), mtp = "fixed_sequence"),
         events = c(pfs = 300, os = 220))
#> Group sequential log-rank design with two endpoints
#>   Endpoints: PFS, then OS (fixed sequence, overall); looks driven by PFS events and OS events
#>   Sample size: 450; accrual duration: 18; final analysis at: 23.05
#>   Power: PFS 0.9387, OS 0.5452; both 0.5452; at least one 0.9387
#>   FWER under global null: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.025 (binding)
#>  endpoint look  time events info_frac z_upper  p_upper hr_upper z_lower
#>       PFS    1 18.62    300    1.0000   1.960 0.025000   0.7975   1.960
#>        OS    1 18.62    163    0.7407   2.357 0.009207   0.6912    -Inf
#>        OS    2 23.05    220    1.0000   2.009 0.022243   0.7626   2.009
#>  hr_lower prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>    0.7975     0.9387          0    0.9387
#>        NA     0.2966          0    0.2966
#>    0.7626     0.2486          0    0.5452

Validation

The tests compare the results with an independent Python implementation (inst/validation/python/, using matrix exponentials and adaptive quadrature) and, when the packages are installed, with gsDesign, gsDesign2, rpact and lrstat.

The scripts in inst/reproduce/ recompute sample sizes, numbers of events, analysis times, bounds and powers printed in 16 sources (articles and a statistical analysis plan). The scripts in inst/validation/ compare the package with patient-level simulations of 15 scenarios (FastSurvival and a Python simulation; PFS and OS analyzed together in 6 of them, switching from a calendar time in 3), with the covariance estimator of Danzer et al. (2025) applied to large simulated trials under the null hypothesis, with the package PWEALL in 8 designs, and with the decisions of lrstat::fseqbon() in 3 designs with recycling of the level. Each folder is run by its run_all.R, which judges every value as PASS (the criterion is met), EXPLAINED (the criterion is met after a registered explanation, such as an apparent misprint), FAIL, or INFO (not judged: a published value computed by a method that the package does not reproduce, or an asymptotic approximation compared with simulation):

Folder PASS EXPLAINED FAIL INFO Total
inst/reproduce/ 257 79 0 191 527
inst/validation/ 1317 0 0 2128 3445

run_all.R also multiplies the compared values by 1.1 and checks that the judgments change as expected. The criteria are described in the README.md of each folder and the registered explanations in its explained.csv. Every compared value is listed with its judgment in results/summary.csv, and results/summary.md summarizes the results. FastSurvival, PWEALL and lrstat (0.3.4 or later) are needed only to rerun inst/validation/.
